import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def _norm_sku(s):
    if pd.isna(s):
        return np.nan
    return str(s).strip().upper()


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    orders = inputs["orders"].copy()
    price_list = inputs["price_list"].copy()

    # ---- expression: sku_norm = UPPER(TRIM(sku)) ----
    orders = orders.reset_index(drop=True)
    orders["_row_id"] = orders.index
    orders["sku_norm"] = orders["sku"].apply(_norm_sku)

    price_list = price_list.copy()
    price_list["_sku_norm_lkp"] = price_list["sku"].apply(_norm_sku)

    # ---- lookup ----
    # NULL sku_norm never matches -> only consider rows with non-null sku_norm
    valid_orders = orders[orders["sku_norm"].notna()]

    if len(valid_orders) > 0 and len(price_list) > 0:
        merged = valid_orders.merge(
            price_list,
            left_on="sku_norm",
            right_on="_sku_norm_lkp",
            suffixes=("", "_pl"),
        )
        # condition: valid_from <= order_date
        merged = merged[merged["valid_from"] <= merged["order_date"]]

        if len(merged) > 0:
            # multiple match tie-break: GREATEST valid_from, then LOWEST list_id
            merged = merged.sort_values(
                ["_row_id", "valid_from", "list_id"],
                ascending=[True, False, True],
                kind="mergesort",
            )
            best = merged.drop_duplicates(subset="_row_id", keep="first")
            best = best[["_row_id", "unit_price"]]
        else:
            best = pd.DataFrame(columns=["_row_id", "unit_price"])
    else:
        best = pd.DataFrame(columns=["_row_id", "unit_price"])

    result = orders.merge(best, on="_row_id", how="left")
